title: U.S. Senate · Rhode Island

context.text: This is the Class II U.S. Senate seat held by Jack Reed, who first took office in 1997. Reed defeated Connor Burbridge and Luis Daniel Muñoz in the September 9, 2026 Democratic primary, 76.8%-13.5%-9.7%. Raymond McKay ran unopposed for the Republican nomination after Allen Waters withdrew. Michael Bahry is running as an independent; a fourth candidate, Jon Lindley (independent), withdrew or was disqualified before the general election.

summary.text: Jack Reed is the Democratic incumbent seeking a sixth term in the U.S. Senate. A Cranston native and West Point graduate, he served as an Army officer, practiced banking and securities law, and served in the Rhode Island State Senate and the U.S. House before being elected to the Senate in 1996. He is the ranking member of the Senate Armed Services Committee.

background.text: Born and raised in Cranston, Rhode Island, according to his Senate office; his father was a World War II veteran and school custodial supervisor and his mother a homemaker. Ballotpedia lists his birthplace as Providence, in 1949.
Attended St. Matthew's Elementary School and graduated from La Salle Academy in Providence.
Graduated from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point in 1971, earned a master's degree in public policy from Harvard's Kennedy School in 1973, and a J.D. from Harvard Law School in 1982.

Served in the 82nd Airborne Division as an infantry platoon leader, company commander and battalion staff officer, then taught economics and international relations at West Point as an associate professor. He left active duty as a captain in 1979 and served in the Army Reserves until 1991, leaving as a major.
Practiced law after law school, first at Sutherland, Asbill & Brennan and then at Edwards & Angell in Providence, specializing in banking and securities law and doing pro bono work for Amos House.
Served three terms in the Rhode Island State Senate (1985-1991).
Elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in 1990 and served three terms from 1991 to 1997, representing Rhode Island's 2nd District.
Elected to the U.S. Senate in 1996 to succeed Claiborne Pell and has served since 1997. He is ranking member of the Armed Services Committee and a senior member of the Appropriations Committee.

According to his Senate office, he was part of the bipartisan group that drafted the CARES Act and wrote provisions of the 2010 Wall Street reform law; he and his wife, Julia Hart Reed, have a daughter, Emily.

record.text: For the 2025-2026 Congress, serves as Ranking Member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, Ranking Member of the Appropriations Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government, and a member of the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs and the Select Committee on Intelligence.
Chaired the Senate Armed Services Committee and the Appropriations Subcommittee on the Legislative Branch during the 2023-2024 Congress.

candidates.name: Raymond McKay

summary.text: Raymond McKay is the Republican nominee. A Warwick resident and native of Providence, he served in the U.S. Army from 1981 to 1992 and then worked 26 years as the City of Warwick's network and telecommunications manager. He lost the 2024 Republican primary for the other Rhode Island Senate seat and is running on a theme he calls "Right Direction Right Now."

background.text: Born in Providence, Rhode Island, on October 11, 1960, and graduated from Hope High School. According to his campaign website, he lives in Warwick and has four children and 13 grandchildren.

Served in the U.S. Army from 1981 to 1992, working on electronic maintenance for the Pershing missile system in West Germany and later training as a programmer at Fort Gordon, Georgia; discharged at the rank of Sergeant.
Worked for 26 years as the network and telecommunications manager for the City of Warwick.

Describes himself as a grassroots political activist since 2000 who has volunteered on local, state and national campaigns and worked as a campaign manager on select Rhode Island races. His first run for office was in 1998 for the Rhode Island State Senate.
Served as president of the Rhode Island Republican Assembly for 10 years.
Ran in the September 10, 2024, Republican primary for U.S. Senate, losing to Patricia Morgan. He advanced from the September 9, 2026, Republican primary to the general election.

priorities.text: Curbing federal government spending, which he says drives inflation and economic pressure on Rhode Islanders.
Securing the border and enforcing immigration law.
Strengthening Social Security and Medicare, and supporting veterans and the military.

positions.summary: Says the country must secure its borders and enforce its laws.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and priorities are drawn from McKay's 2024 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (for a prior run for this same seat); he has not completed a 2026 survey and no updated policy page was found on his 2026 campaign site.

summary.text: Michael Bahry is an independent candidate for U.S. Senate. A Rhode Island native, he worked as a laborer, carpenter and construction executive and founded a Providence nonprofit before returning to school for two master's degrees in theology and biblical studies. He is running on ending U.S. involvement in foreign wars and on congressional term limits.

background.text: According to his campaign website, a native Rhode Islander, married for over 40 years, with two children and four grandchildren.
His career spanned roles as a laborer, carpenter, construction executive and business owner, including running a commercial construction company.
Founded the nonprofit Fifty-Three: Five in 2014, which provides food, fellowship and support to families and the homeless in Providence, and speaks monthly at the Providence Rescue Mission.
At age 53 returned to college, earning a Master of Theological Studies (2017) and a Master of Arts in Biblical Studies (2022) from Providence College.

Teaches theology at Salve Regina University and is the author of the book Hell Is a Bad Word, according to his campaign website. He is a lector and finance committee member at Our Lady of Loreto Church.

priorities.text: Ending U.S. participation in what he calls "endless wars," saying it makes the world less safe rather than more.
Running as an independent so he can vote issue-by-issue without party loyalty.
Addressing the national debt, which he says has been driven up by career politicians.

positions.summary: Calls the war in Gaza a tragedy and campaigns for peace rather than continued military involvement in the conflict.
